scope: Proposition 4.2 (Positive normal transfer) of the manuscript “Gaussian free-field limits of weighted integer Lipschitz heights” (preprints/Gaussian-free-field-limits-of-weighted-integer-Lipschitz-heights-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 232 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3dae0156982e5d20), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 28. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let ℓ be any row of lattice sites parallel to one of the three unoriented nearest-neighbor directions, and choose one of its closed half-planes. The plane pair is reflection positive across ℓ. The assertion remains valid after adjoining any finite collection of fields Zs(u) = Us exp{is(H(u) − H(o))}, (4.2) where the Us are independent unit-circle Haar variables, independent of the pair, and o is any anchor. More precisely, let θℓ act on observables by spatial reflection, and take local functions supported in the chosen half-plane, whose height differences are evaluated along paths in that half-plane. Then ⟨F, G⟩ℓ = E  θℓF G  is a positive semidefinite Hermitian form. In its quotient completion, translation farther into the half-plane by the pure normal vector of length √ 3 is a positive self-adjoint contraction S. Unit translation along the row is a commuting unitary U. At mesh δ the normal step is √ 3δ.
